steps.what: Teach independent living techniques suited to the client's visual impairment

tasks.design: Retain demonstration and supervised practice of accessible eating, personal management and care routines. Existing {DOCS} care instructions remain authoritative; teaching access techniques does not authorise changes to medicines or diabetes treatment.
tasks.previous_blocker: A technique must work with the client's actual tools, vision and capabilities.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated substitute for supervised daily-living instruction is supplied in the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Preventing practical errors while preserving independence.
tasks.human_edge: Observe real performance and adapt the teaching to the person.

reach.task: Clarify safe medication and diabetes care instructions
reach.learn: Escalate clinical treatment questions while teaching accessible routines

evidence.claim: Accessible routine instruction requires individual practice and does not itself change treatment; no practical teaching saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is therapist teaching of access techniques, excluding treatment decisions, routine care delivery and client practice outside sessions.
The responsible care practitioner produces treatment instructions under existing care processes; no automatic medication decisions or machine-ready dose fields are assumed.
Therapist observation and clarification remain fully counted. Native accessible instructions are preferred; no new service upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Can the client demonstrate the routine safely with the tools actually used at home?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Demonstration, observation and feedback retain all time; no clinical treatment or caregiver time enters the saving.
